title: Revise rerank response contract for stable continuations, per-item provenance, and scalable pagination
creator: Asha Patel
description: Context: Our current rerank endpoint has surfaced multiple client issues: unstable ordering when clients page with different page sizes, lack of deterministic tie-breaking on equal scores, opaque continuation tokens, and insufficient per-item provenance for downstream debugging. This ticket proposes a revised response contract that makes continuations stable across page sizes, adds explicit per-item provenance and score breakdowns, and scales to large candidate sets without forcing the server to materialize giant sorted lists in memory. Goals: 1) Ensure deterministic ordering across pages and page sizes for a given scoring snapshot; 2) Provide clear continuation tokens that let clients fetch next pages consistently even with transient corpus changes; 3) Surface provenance (source id, embedding snapshot id, score components) so clients can make informed decisions; 4) Keep server memory and CPU usage bounded with large candidate pools; 5) Maintain backward compatibility for basic clients.
proposal_summary: Introduce a lightweight continuation token that encodes: (a) snapshot_id of embeddings/scorer, (b) last_item_sort_key, (c) stable_seed used for deterministic tie-breaks, and (d) scorer_version. Change top_k semantics: 'top_k' requests a global bound on number of results to return across pagination, while 'page_size' controls per-response count; allow 'windowed_mode' where server performs windowed selection to avoid full sort. Add a new 'provenance' object per item including source_id, embedding_snapshot, raw_score, normalized_score, score_breakdown (comma-delimited string for compatibility), and a 'stability_hash' field used as tie-breaker. Emit observability headers (X-Rerank-Queue-Time, X-Rerank-Compute-Time, X-Rerank-Snapshot-ID).
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: 1) Full stable ordering via global sort: simplest for clients but requires materializing/sorting entire candidate set (O(n log n)) and high memory for large n — rejected for high-scale customers. 2) Stateful cursor retained on server: would allow opaque cursors tied to server memory but complicates autoscaling and redis cleanup. 3) Proposed approach (stateless continuation + stable_seed + snapshot_id): slightly more complex token semantics but scales and aligns with our stateless routing model. 4) Allow clients to opt-in to strict consistency via 'consistency=strong' flag (server may reject for huge candidate sets).
acceptance_criteria: 1) For a fixed snapshot_id and stable_seed, paging with different page_size values must produce a non-overlapping, deterministic ordering equivalent to slicing the globally sorted list. 2) Continuation token must be opaque but decodable by server to validate snapshot mismatch and return clear 'snapshot_mismatch' error when appropriate. 3) Each item in response must include 'source_id', 'embedding_snapshot', 'raw_score', 'normalized_score', and 'score_breakdown' fields. 4) API must expose headers for queue and compute time. 5) Unit and integration tests covering small and large candidate sets, ties, and concurrent updates. 6) P95 latency for top_k<=10, page_size<=10 must remain <=120ms under normal load (see outcome_metrics).
outcome_metrics:
- P95 end-to-end latency (top_k<=10, page_size<=10): target < 120ms
- P99 latency: monitored, expect < 450ms for common workloads
- Increase in requests that use pagination: metric to track adoption
- Reduction in customer-reported ordering bugs by 90% for clients using snapshot_id
- Memory usage per request: bounded; no O(n) allocations for n>50k candidates
implementation_notes: - Add 'snapshot_id' to request schema (optional). Server returns current snapshot_id when missing. - Continuation token format: base64(JSON: {snapshot_id, last_sort_key, stable_seed, scorer_version}). Tokens capped at 2KB. - Implement deterministic tie-breaker: stable_sort_key = (primary_score, stable_seed XOR hash(item_id)). Use 64-bit hash to keep keys compact. - Windowed selection: implement reservoir-like selection where server computes top window (page_size * W) then deterministic local sort; default W=4 for large candidate pools. - Streaming: support returning partial pages while computing next window to reduce tail latency. - Observability: emit X-Rerank-Queue-Time and X-Rerank-Compute-Time headers and log per-request candidate_count, window_size, and snapshot_id to tracing system. - Backwards compatibility: if client omits 'page_size' and 'snapshot_id', behave as current API but include 'deprecation_notice' in response body for future removal.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in): release new contract behind 'rerank_v2' feature flag and document snapshot_id usage. Provide SDK helpers to generate/consume continuation tokens. Phase 2 (adoption): encourage clients to pass snapshot_id for strict stability; monitor usage and bug reports. Phase 3 (opt-out older contract): after ~3 months and client migrations, set rerank_v2 as default and keep legacy for enterprise only. Provide scripts to re-encode existing cursors and a migration FAQ. Update SDKs (python/node) with examples.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for continuation token encoding/decoding, tie-breaker behavior, and ordering invariants under variable page sizes.
- Integration tests: run rerank over synthetic candidate sets with induced ties, and assert deterministic paging behavior.
- Load tests: candidate pools of 10k, 100k, 1M to validate memory/CPU bounds for windowed_mode.
- Canary: deploy to staging and run customer-sim workloads; compare ordering against full-sort baseline.
- Regression tests: verify existing clients without snapshot_id continue to get compatible responses.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement behind feature flag 'rerank_v2'. 2) Internal canary with infra and search platform teams. 3) Open beta for select customers (notify via account managers). 4) Monitor telemetry for ordering errors, latency, and memory usage for two weeks. 5) Gradual ramp to all tenants. 6) Deprecate legacy cursor after 12 weeks.

notes_and_discussion:
2026-03-05: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed on snapshot_id approach and stateless continuations (Asha, Lucas, Priya, Marco).
2026-03-07: Design review: asked to cap token size and ensure token revocation is possible via snapshot expiration (Priya).
2026-03-10: Performance spike observed in prototype when candidate_count ~200k; decided to increase window multiplier default and add streaming partial responses (Marco).
2026-03-12: PM asked for clear migration docs and SDK helpers; recording as action items.
Open questions: Should 'top_k' be enforced server-side as absolute cap across pages or advisory? (We enforce as cap when snapshot_id provided). How to handle updates to scorer_version mid-pagination? We surface 'scorer_version' in continuation and return 'snapshot_mismatch' if changed.

customer_communication_snippet: We're introducing an improved rerank response contract that makes paging stable and adds per-item provenance. You can opt in today by setting 'rerank_v2=true' in your request. If you rely on strict ordering, pass the 'snapshot_id' to pin a scoring snapshot. See the migration guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RERANK/Migration+Guide
final_comments: This design balances client ergonomics and server scalability. The most fragile part is token validity across frequent embedding updates; we'll mitigate with snapshot TTLs and clear error messages. Expect a follow-up ticket to support server-side pinning for enterprise customers who want guaranteed long-lived cursors.
